## Chapter Ten

War



The next month went by uneventfully, the Latino’s finally had been released from there room, but there were no more attempts on Lucas and hopefully he thought the Warden had gotten it out of his system. A few messages had come through the old man from Dyson but aside from that, things had seemed to settle down. Though looking back Lucas should have known better.



He continued to train and read, and Polar Bear was actually getting to the point where his loosing wasn’t completely embarrassing, and Lucas had to grudgingly agree he was getting better.



They made there way to the mess hall as they did everyday, but something didn’t seem right, Lucas noticed quite a few glances coming his way almost to the point where he had begun to get paranoid. Something was up. The hair on the back of his neck was sticking straight up by the time they had reached the mess hall, getting his chow he sat at the same table, but today he sat so he could watch most of the room.



Everyone continued to eat as usual, but again he could see glances being shot his way. “Anyone hear anything?” he asked One Time and Re Run who had just sat down. The confused look on their faces told him everything he needed to know. The four of them ate their food and no one commented on the odd looks and whispers they were getting from the other tables.



Before they had finished eating Macready, one of the regulars in Downtown walked over and nodded at the four of them. “You guys have clean up today” he said and then continued on. It wasn’t unusual that they would get clean up, but it was that all four of them would be assigned at once, they usually only ever allowed two at a time in the mess after eating to clean up. Macready didn’t seem bothered by the request, and as far as Lucas knew it was straight up, they had a few crooked guards and most of them switched up too often to really get to know them , but Macready had been assigned to downtown going on a month now, spend time with someone that long , seeing them pretty much every day you could develop at least a semi accurate opinion of them.



They waited for everyone to leave the mess and then began the tasks of wiping the tables, collecting trays and mopping the floor, about halfway through another guard came in, this one Lucas didn’t know and came over to him personally. “You, back to your cell, the rest, finish cleaning up” he stated and before he could walk away Lucas spoke up “Why?” he asked , this being the second odd request he had gotten today.



The guard turned around with a hard look on his face, “Look, I just pass the messages they tell me, I don’t ask questions , you should learn from that example and stop annoying me, now go back to downtown convict” the guard said, poking Lucas in the chest hard enough to cause him to wince. He looked at his friends, all giving him a worried look, and headed back to his cell. He didn’t like it, in fact he was sure that going down the hall someone would have jumped out and attacked him, but the hall was clear, and he made to the door of downtown without any issues.



Lucas hit the button and waited for the door to buzz open. As soon as it did, he stepped into the common area and stopped dead in his tracks. Everything was wrong, looking around he could see the cell doors opened and the lights off, he also noticed no guards, drone or cameras were on.



The hair on the back of his neck rose straight up as he cautiously stepped into the large dark room.



He didn’t see the fist before it slammed into the side of his face, sending him careening for the floor. He hit the concrete hard and turned his head to see a group of eight men, he couldn’t see their faces, just the silhouettes as the door closed, bringing the room closer to total darkness. He tried to life himself but was put back down by a foot on his back, and then the kicking began, no one spoke a word feet pulled back and slammed into his side sending bright lances of pain along his sides.



He curled into a ball trying to protect his body as the blows continued to reign down upon him. Hit after hit, and blow after blow the lances of pain turned into a steady stream, He screamed before someone slammed a fist into his mouth sending a few teeth down his throat causing Lucas to choke. I am going to die he thought, unable to bring himself to any sort of defensive position under the onslaught.



He wasn’t sure how long it lasted, or at one point someone found him, he just remembered voices, alarmed voices, then nothing.



He woke some time later back in the med bay, the sun had not risen so he could only assume it was still night time. With his one half swollen eye he looked over the other beds to see only a few people sleeping deeply. Lucas tried to assess the damage and shifted in bed, as soon as he moved a wash of bright white pain shot up into his head he whimpered and settled back in the bed oh they did a number he thought, moving his arms and legs, realizing they were all wrapped in casts. He brought his hand to his face to feel the wrappings covering half his head. “They couldn’t save the right eye, I’m sorry” came a familiar voice from the darkness. A small red light illuminated from his left revealing a silent and stalwart Dyson, standing next to his bed. The old man looked much older than Lucas remembered. His face looked sympathetic, something he had never seen for as long as he had known them. This made Lucas more concerned than ever. “Am I okay?” he asked urgently, not really wanting to know the answer. Dyson nodded “Aside from your eye, everything else will heal, but we have bigger problems then your injury” he said still low enough so only Lucas could hear him. The drugs they pumped into his system still had Lucas groggy, making it difficult to concentrate. “How did you get in here?” he asked his older friend.



Dyson sat on the edge of the bed, “it’s a long story and we don’t have a lot of time, at some point, someone will tell it to you but here is the stripped-down version, to save time” he said. “If they knew who I was then I would be summarily dragged into the exercise yard and shot, I have friends in here so to some limited extent, I can get things done, I can find out things, and Lucas, what I have found is not good for you kid” he said and then locked a stare with Lucas’s one good eye.



“Someone wants you dead, I can imagine its someone from the company who your father worked for, your father was setup, he was framed for embezzlement, though if they knew what he was really up to he still would have been executed. However, someone high up in the Department of Finance feels even though it’s been years, you’re somehow a liability, so you have been ordered killed” Dyson said. Lucas gasped, what the hell he thought, what I could I possibly know that someone would want me dead? He thought to himself. “The important thing is I need you alive, but if you stay here, they will kill you and there is nothing either of us can do about it”. Dyson continued.



Dyson leaned closer “So tonight, you are going to die”.



The nurse came in for her morning shift and began to check the charts hovering over the foot of the beds. The holographic view allowed the nurse to see all the patient’s vitals and any notes the doctor had left for them. Walking along the line she heard a low alarm coming from one of the beds. With a confused look she followed the sound to the bed of the young man who had come in the night before severely beaten. His vitals were all flatlined and according to the computer that monitored him, he was dead.



Hurrying back to the desk the nurse rang the doctor on duty who showed up not five minutes later. It took only as few moments to confirm the inmate as deceased and call down for a morgue transport.



The doctor reviewed the paperwork as the body was packed into a transport container “You guys got here fast, I only called down like two minutes ago” the young night shift doctor said, making conversation as he put the final signatures on the order. A large grey-haired man turned and smiled at the doctor “slow night doc” he said casually.



As the orderly took a last look at the dead body of Lucas Christian before closing the lid.



As the truck pulled away from the prison gates a thumping was heard from the lid of the transport coffin, starting erratically and quiet but quickly speeding up as the beating turned frantic. “Jesus Job, can you just shut him up until we get to the drop off point” said the young man as he begins to lift the transport vehicle into the skyway. Job grumbled and said something about the driver’s mother but climbed over the seat and slapped his hand on the coffin lid yelling to make sure his quarry could hear him. “Hey, shut the fuck up, we will get you out when we get to the drop off location” and then he tried to get back into the front but after several tries, gave up and chose to sit in the side fold down seat of the transport ambulance.



The boxy white and red ambulance floated down into the ruins of what was once called the Shockoe district in Richmond, between the Railroad Y ruins and what was left of the farmers market the vehicle settled down with a quiet thump. Three men came out of the shadows of the ruins their heads on swivels as they approached the idling vehicle.



The young driver got out and handed the oldest of the three something, it quickly disappeared into his pocket. As the driver began to walk away towards the old state capitol up the street, the three men under cover of darkness opened the rear doors and grabbed the large metal coffin. The gruff orderly got out after, nodding at the three he too began to walk away in a different direction.



The case was carried into the old ruins of the Railroad Y building, the husk of the old YMCA building turned apartments had long since eroded into a single story with no roof. As they made their way into the shell of the structure, they put the coffin down in a corner, the oldest of the three pushed a code into the pad on the lid and stood back, as all three waited.



Lucas heard the lid beep and then felt it give under his pushing. He slowly raised the lid to reveal an overweight bearded elderly man with an infectious smile standing there. As Lucas continued to push the lid off, he noticed the man’s other two companions, both standing in the shadow, so he couldn’t see their faces, but neither as friendly looking as this big bear of a man.



The large man held out a massive hand to Lucas helping him out of the coffin. “Congratulations, you are now dead” the man said laughing, though it sounded more like someone was trying to shave a coke can on a cheese grater, it was still pleasant in its own way. “Um, thank you I guess” Lucas answered, his legs unsteady under him. The old man caught him and steadied him on his feet. “Careful , the drugs they gave you will wear off and it did stop your heart for a moment, give it a little time , we don’t have to move quite yet my friend” the man soothed.



Lucas looked around the destroyed building and took in a long breath, this was the first breath of free air he had breathed in close to four years. He shook with fright and excitement, when Dyson had told him the plan, he went along but honestly, he thought the chances of success were slim. Yet here he was. Lucas sat down on the edge of his coffin letting out a sigh, his muscles felt like he had been running for hours. Lucas studied the profile of dilapidated buildings running in front of the one he currently hid in, at one time it must have been a nice neighborhood he thought, shaking his head, a lot had been destroyed when the corporations took over. “So, what’s the plan guys?” Lucas croaked, he cleared his throat and tried again with no success. The large bearded man clapped him on the back., “Don’t worry kid, Dyson told me to take real good care of you, you must have left quite an impression” he said leaning in so Lucas could see his face from the little bit of light coming through the broken window.



He studied the bandage over Lucas’s eye and his normally happy expression fell a little “had a bad time in there huh” he asked, Lucas could see the empathy, actual empathy In the man’s face. He nodded and lowered his head, it had been a long time since he had seen empathy he thought. “I can’t give you the specifics, but we have to make you disappear, we are going to stick you in a safe house until we can get ahold of the doctor” he started, and Lucas stopped him “What doctor?” he asked confused.



The old man stopped and locked eyes with Lucas, he fidgeted with the zipper on his jacket for a moment and then sighed. “I figured Dyson would have covered this with you, they have cameras everywhere kid and your dead, we need to alter your face otherwise you will be back in prison answering some very uncomfortable questions for us if we don’t” he stated. Shaking his head he looked down “I don’t even really know who you guys are, Dyson didn’t really cover a whole lot” he said , realizing he didn’t have a choice about the face, they were right. The old man squatted down, bringing his face to Lucas’s level “Listen kid, I know its going to be hard , but I am going to help get you through this, my name is Job, like the bible guy” he said another infectious grin spreading across his face as he held out his hand for Lucas. Lucas couldn’t help it, a matching grin appeared on his face and he took the massive mit “Good to meet you, Im Lucas” he answered.



Before they could continue the conversation, one of the other two leaned in from the shadows, giving Lucas a look at the ebony face and gold teeth for the first time. “We gots to go, now” he said , his face worried and serious. Job just nodded “Okay, pull the car around” he said to the other, who walked towards the front of the building.



Lucas heard a horn but before he could get up to join the other two, Job put a hand on his shoulder “I need you to wear this until we get to the safe house” he said pulling what looked like a fancy dog collar out of his Jacket pocket. Lucas looked at it confused and then back at Job “This will obscure you face for the cameras and drones, we don’t need the system identifying you.” He said, nodding Lucas put on the collar and as he was lowering his arms , Job put a large wrist clamp over his right arm. Started Lucas jerked back causing Job to put up both his hands “Easy kid, this just blocks the signal from your identity chip” He sighed and then let Job ensure that the wrist cuff was on tightly. Lucas chided himself, he had forgotten about that, every child had one injected, the chip allowed any system to identify you, it’s how you paid for things, it’s how you got into buildings, used trains, did anything, you no longer carried cash, or identification, the chip was that for everyone. And Job was right, it sent out a low power RF signal that drones could pick up and it wouldn’t do to have a computer telling people he was up and walking around down here when he was supposed to be dead”.



They picked their way through the debris of the once stately apartments and onto the street where a black four door sedan sat idling, once everyone was in, the car lifted off, heading away from the city towards the south. No one spoke as they flew, Lucas getting his first look at the world since being incarcerated was happy just to sit here and watch the scenery.



They flew for over an hour south, the lights of the city and suburbs giving way to the blackness of the rural areas of Virginia. The skyway at this time has very little traffic allowing Lucas a good few of the black rolling landscape below. After a while the car descended , coming to land infront of an old dilapidated farm house. Everyone exited the vehicle and Job motioned for him to follow him into the building, the other two walked a little ways out into the yard as a delivery truck desenced in front of them. Once it had landed the two who had accompanied Job got it and it lifted off, both gone without a word. This didn’t seem to bother the big man, as he laid a hand on Lucas’s shoulder to help him inside.



The inside didn’t look much better than the outside had, the house was dirty with water stains over the ceiling, a small lamp illuminated the room, showing a sleeping bag and back pack in the corner. He looked at job arching his unbandaged eye. Job gave him an apologetic expression and shrugged “best we could do on short notice, but it will only be for a few days” he assured his ward.



As Lucas settled down on top of the sleeping back, Job went outside to rustle up some wood, the house was cold, and the October winds could be heard caressing the outside of the old farmhouse. When Job had returned, he spent a few moments lighting the old fireplace and getting it burning.



After a few moments Lucas was able to remove his Jacket as the head radiating from the large fireplace warmed the room. “I need you to stay here, stay away from the windows and don’t answer the door, I need to go and get things ready but I will be back in a few days, keep the collar and the bracelet on at all times, I don’t expect a drone or police out this way, but you never know” Job said getting up and heading for the door. “Job” Lucas called getting the big man’s attention. “Thanks, for all this” he said getting a big smile from the old man. “Don’t thank me, Dyson was insistent, I don’t know what he needs from you son, but he is moving mountains for you right now” he finished and left Lucas to think on that. Dyson didn’t strike him as sentimental, so it was quite possible his old prison buddy did need something, just hadn’t told Lucas what it was yet. He spent a fitful night sleeping in the old drafty house, half expecting the police to beat down the door and drag him back to prison. At about three o’clock in the morning he finally gave up sleeping, he checked the collar and the wrist shackle to ensure they were snug and leaned back against the peeling wallpapered wall. He tied to piece together what he knew, he knew his father worked with Dyson, Dyson wanted something that he thought Lucas was the only one who could give it to him and he was willing to go through a lot of trouble to ensure he stayed alive. A lot of his innocence had been sacrificed during his time at prison, he thought more like a cynical forty-year-old then a bright eyed twenty-six that he actually was.



He couldn’t figure Dyson’s angle and the longer he thought about it the more it frustrated him. An hour later he gave up and went searching the house for any food realizing he was ravenous. After searching the cabinets and the ancient refrigerator, he finally remembered the pack next to the sleeping back and began to rummage through it, producing a few cans of spaghetti and some corn beef hash. He also came out with a small hunting knife and proceeded to spend twenty minutes jabbing at the can until he had enough of the top open, he could get to the food, as long as he carefully avoided the jagged edges. He ate the entire can of corn beef hash cold, Lucas didn’t care after prison food, this was like eating a dinner at a five-star restaurant. He closed his eyes enjoying something that tasted somewhat like meat for the first time in years. Despite Job’s warning as soon as the sun came up , Lucas went outside to collect more firewood and get a good lay of the land, if something happened and the police did show up, he needed an escape route , the training that he had Received at Dyson’s hands was now second nature and he spent the morning planning exfiltration strategies should the police show up.



As the sun started to set on the old farmstead, Lucas sat on the sleeping back staring at the large stack of wood he had collected and at the roaring fire in the old stone fireplace. He felt content, as if he could stay here the rest of his life , outside of the normal everyday bustle. Its amazing he thought, going to prison has allowed him to simplify his existence, before he had been concerned with social media, going to movies , restaurants, girls and so many other things that cluttered up his day, now, he was perfectly happy with a roaring fire and a place to sleep.



He drifted off an hour later, his dreams plagued with shadowy figures hovered over him, inflicting pain.



He awoke with a start around three in the morning again, this time his eye ached causing an oncoming migraine, Lucas sifted through the bag coming out with new bandages and some aspirin, He took twelve of the pills and tried unsuccessfully to rebandage his eye.  Searching the house, he found a dirty mirror shard and got a shock when he looked at his face wound for the first time, the eye was gone, the doctor had sutured up the eyelid and feeling around he could feel something in the orbit, probably something to keep it from deflating he thought. The suture job was neat but the scarring around the area looked bad, he didn’t know if when Job had his face changed, they would fix that. Shaking his head he put down the mirror and leaned his head back against the wall, did it really matter, isn’t his ability to stay free more important then some vain attempt at fixing a scar he chided himself.



His thoughts were interrupted when he heard a rustling coming from outside, Lucas held his breath for a moment reaching out with his ears to try and isolate the location of the sound. After a few moments he heard it again.  Picking up the knife that he had used to open the can he crawled towards the broken and covered window as quietly as possible. The rustling came again and Lucas stopped halfway across the floor, holding his breath and listening again. This time it was closer, sounding like it was coming from right outside the window.  He made his way over to the closed window and then slid along the wall to the doorway. Lucas winced as he turned the knob on the door swinging it inward and it let out a long quiet groan. He peaked his head to the right but couldn’t see anything. Getting up, he crouch walked over to the window, his head on a turret as he surveyed the yard looking for any vehicles or anything out of place. He couldn’t see anything that hadn’t been there when he went inside earlier. Lucas reached the bush and began to step towards the window when something large and furry burst from under the shrubbery, chittering in protest as it ran across the yard. His heart hammering, Lucas dropped onto one knee to catch his breath, laughing as the Racoon continued to waddle run back towards the tree line.



He got up, tossing a stick after the offending animal, though still laughing and returned inside to the warm room, after stoking the fire he quickly fell back asleep dreaming about racoons, prison cells and bushes.



He awoke with a start when he heard a vehicle descending outside. Lucas jumped up and grabbed the backpack, he quickly put the loose cans and the knife inside and then made his way over to the window, leaning against the wall, he tried to spy the vehicle using an open slit between the window covering and the broken pane , but he couldn’t get a good look at it. “Screw this” he said and headed for the back door. After ensuring no one was about to beat it down, he walked in a crouch around the house , when he came to the edge , using his good eye he peaked round the corner to see Job getting out of the Black car and lumbering over to the door. Lucas sighed and tried to put his heart back into his chest. After a minute he rose and came around the side of the house waving at the big man. “How are you today?” Job asked, noticing the backpack and nodding at it. “Sorry to scare you, but I told you I would be back today” he said semi apologetically. Lucas smiled and nodded, he had in fact told him that. “What’s the plan Job” Lucas asked now all business, he was tired of playing the waiting game and to be honest with himself feeling just a little stir crazy despite his thoughts of living the simple life. Turns out he still loved people, who knew he thought a wry smile spreading across his face at the thought.



Job looked questioningly at him Lucas just waved him off, he didn’t need to explain to him that he might be a little jumpy after being in prison for over four years.



“We are moving your location, everything is lined up with the doctor, he will fix you up and change your face so facial recognition won’t be able to identify you” Job said motioning Lucas to the car. He took one more look at the old farm house and mentally said his goodbyes, walking over to the car he put the back pack in the rear and sat shotgun as the car lifted into the skyway.  As the car lifted off Job talked about trivial things, the man didn’t seem to like silence when he was around, Lucas thought smiling, he enjoyed listening to the old man talk about the weather, his dogs or any other subject,it had the air of normalcy, and that was something that Lucas had been lacking for years.



The car turned east along the skyway and jumped into the steady traffic flow with the other cars sharing their journey towards the coast. Long before they got there however, the big car descended towards a large house in a suburban neighborhood, each property having about five acres each, the neighborhood looked very affluent, unlike the cities which were broken out into blocks for executives and workers, out here you would only find top level management and rich specialists.
